clue.text: Interfere with doctor in case

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, a standard abbreviation for a doctor
lest means in case, as in 'take a coat lest it rain'

explanation.surface: Someone meddles with a physician who is on a case.
explanation.definitionFit: To molest is to pester or interfere with someone, the older and milder sense of the verb.

clue.text: Complaint of girl about US city

indicators.note: the girl's name goes round the city abbreviation

parts.note: Maria is a girl's name
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A girl grumbles about an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaria is a disease, and complaint is a common word for an illness.

clue.text: Flower festival finally in front and fashionable

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of festival

parts.note: up means ahead or in front, as in two goals up
in means fashionable, as in the in thing

explanation.surface: A bloom wins a festival, coming out ahead and stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a garden plant with tall spikes of pea-like blooms.

clue.text: See 17
Very nearly a fish if I 'ad replaced plate

indicators.note: the letter I in the fish is swapped out for what the plate supplies
the Cockney spelling of had drops its opening aspirate, so the fish loses its leading letter too

parts.note: a halibut is a large flatfish
an L-plate is the learner's plate on a British car, so plate gives L

explanation.surface: A dropped-aitch speaker muses about a fish and a swapped dish, nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: ''ad' signals the dropped H, turning HALIBUT into ALIBUT; 'replaced' then swaps its I for L, giving ALLBUT. An L-plate is the red L sign a British learner driver must display.
explanation.definitionFit: All but is an idiom meaning almost or very nearly, as in 'all but finished'.

clue.text: Latin article with measure of cord

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a yard is a measure of length

explanation.surface: A Latin text comes with a measured length of string.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanyard is a cord worn round the neck or used on a ship for fastening.

clue.text: Such gardens give trouble to Caliban

indicators.note: to trouble the letters is to stir them up into a new order

explanation.surface: Ornamental grounds cause the monster of The Tempest grief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give trouble' rearranges TO CALIBAN. Caliban is the monster in Shakespeare's The Tempest, a play set on an island full of plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanical gardens are the gardens kept for the scientific study of plants, so the word describes such gardens.

clue.text: Water god, leading American writer

indicators.note: leading puts the god in front of the water

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
eau is French for water

explanation.surface: A water deity heads the list as a US author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water god' reads as one deity, but the two words split and 'leading' puts the god before the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry David Thoreau was the American author of Walden.

clue.text: Arab mount for music presenter and mutineer right away

parts.note: a DJ or disc jockey presents music

indicators.note: away says the letter for right is sent off from the mutineer

parts.note: a rebel is one who mutinies

explanation.surface: A disc jockey and a rebel ride off on a mountain in Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes the R from REBEL, leaving EBEL. Mount means a mountain, not a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A djebel or jebel is a hill or mountain in Arab-speaking North Africa and the Middle East.

clue.text: Support actor's union at 16's 19 17 3

parts.note: to clap a performer is to applaud, showing support
a ham is an overacting performer; the possessive adds no letters
a junction is a joining or union of things

explanation.surface: Back a performers' trade union at some event.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spelt out by other entries: BRITAIN's BUSIEST RAILWAY STATION. CLAPHAM JUNCTION in south London handles more trains than any other British station.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapham Junction is famously described as the nation's busiest railway interchange by number of trains.

clue.text: Sultanate, live one, outside series

indicators.note: the verb for living goes round the word for a series, enclosing it

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
a run is a series, as in a run of wins
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sultan's realm, broadcast live, sits beside a series.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a small oil-rich state on Borneo ruled by a sultan.

clue.text: Born a prince with more intelligence

parts.note: b is the standard abbreviation for born in biographies
Prince Rainier III ruled Monaco for over fifty years

explanation.surface: A child born to royalty grows up cleverer.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainier is the comparative of brainy, meaning cleverer or having more intellect.

clue.text: Three little boys may be Georgian

parts.note: Pat is a short boy's name, a diminutive of Patrick
Ron is a short form of Ronald
Al is a short form of Albert or Alan

explanation.surface: Three young lads might pass for natives of Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three little boys' supplies three short names in a row. St George is England's patron saint, so a festival in his honour is patronal; Georgian is not about the era or the country here.
explanation.definitionFit: Patronal means relating to a patron saint, and something Georgian honours Saint George, so a patronal feast may be Georgian.

clue.text: Very bad line here for the mounted

parts.note: rotten means very bad
a row is a line

explanation.surface: A terrible queue awaits those on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotten Row is the sandy track in London's Hyde Park used for horse riding.

clue.text: See 15
Passing remark on love bite — run to police when upset inside

parts.note: love means zero in tennis, which looks like O
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: upset in the sense of overturned, so the police abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police
tum, short for tummy, is one's inside

explanation.surface: A remark about a love bite prompts someone to dash to the police when their stomach is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses the police abbreviation. The surface's upset inside suggests a sick stomach, but inside is simply the tummy.
explanation.definitionFit: Obiter dictum is Latin for a thing said in passing, especially a judge's incidental comment.

clue.text: Educated girl in place of rubbish here

indicators.note: the girl is placed in the receptacle for refuse

parts.note: a bin is where rubbish goes
Rita is the heroine of Willy Russell's play Educating Rita

explanation.surface: A schooled young woman ends up in the rubbish tip.
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Rita is a British play and film in which a hairdresser called Rita gets an education.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain is here for the setter and readers of a British newspaper, so here stands for the country.

clue.text: Where I saw to train layout?

indicators.note: out says the preceding letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A model railway enthusiast asks where they saw how to lay out a train set.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'out' is the tail of layout: the fodder is I SAW TO TRAIN LAY, and 'out' rearranges it. The whole clue also reads as a picture of where trains are set out.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway station is a place where trains stop, so it answers the question where.

clue.text: Composer, sister to one with no daughter

parts.note: a sib is a sibling, here a sister

indicators.note: the second composer is taken without the letter for daughter

parts.note: one refers back to composer: Frederick Delius was an English composer
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A composer is named as sister to another who has no daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' means another composer, DELIUS; 'with no' removes his D for daughter, leaving ELIUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Sibelius was the Finnish composer of Finlandia and seven symphonies.

clue.text: I'm on TV with card about a month back

indicators.note: the card goes round the month

parts.note: a SIM card is the chip card in a mobile phone

indicators.note: back says the month abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: Oct is October

explanation.surface: Someone announces a TV appearance, card in hand, a month back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the month and 'about' puts the phone card round it; the surface's month back is a time, not a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation comedy is a television show, so it could say it is on TV.

clue.text: Second turn for endless rest with most activity

parts.note: B is second, as in B-grade or the second letter
a U-turn gives U for turn

indicators.note: endless removes the final letter of the word for rest

parts.note: a siesta is an afternoon rest

explanation.surface: Another go at a curtailed nap is the busiest option.
explanation.definitionFit: Busiest means most busy, having the most going on.

clue.text: Posh girl keeps posh as a rule

parts.note: U means upper-class, the classic label for posh usage

indicators.note: keeps means the girl's name holds the letter inside it

parts.note: Sally is a girl's name
U again means upper-class or posh

explanation.surface: A well-bred girl holds on to her airs, as she generally does.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U language labels.
explanation.definitionFit: Usually and as a rule both mean normally or in most cases.

clue.text: Intelligence about various lines of booze here

indicators.note: the word for intelligence goes around the jumbled lines

parts.note: wit means intelligence or sharp mental capacity

indicators.note: various suggests the letters of lines take differing arrangements

explanation.surface: Smart remarks about assorted lines in a drinks menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges lines and 'about' puts the intelligence word around the result, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant's wine list is the card where its alcoholic drinks are found.

clue.text: Element of Nature evokes special dislike

parts.note: odium means hatred or strong dislike

explanation.surface: A feature of the natural world provokes particular distaste.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium is a chemical element, a soft reactive metal found throughout nature in salt.

clue.text: Live having died before spring

parts.note: a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Someone lives on, having passed away before springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to reside or live somewhere.

clue.text: Wed without ring? New job possible at length with this concoction

indicators.note: possible hints at a possible rearrangement of all the gathered letters

parts.note: wed gives marry, and without in its old sense of outside sets it round a ring-shaped O
an ell is an old measure of length of about 45 inches

explanation.surface: A ringless wedding and a new job might be cause to whip up a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so MARRY goes round O; 'possible' then rearranges that with NEW, JOB and the ell.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrowbone jelly is an old-fashioned savoury preparation made by simmering beef marrow bones.

clue.text: Town in south-west given just now to north

parts.note: newly means recently or just now

explanation.surface: A west-country town has just recently joined the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Newlyn is a fishing town near Penzance in Cornwall, England's far south-west.

clue.text: Small boy chasing books gets earache

indicators.note: chasing puts the boy behind the books, following them

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the first books of the Bible
Algy is a short boy's name, from Algernon

explanation.surface: A little lad running after his books ends up with a sore ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Otalgia or otalgy is the medical term for pain in the ear.
